page: Amazon Web Services c7i-flex.xlarge is an x86_64 compute-optimized server powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features a dedicated Intel Xeon 8488C processor running at 3.2 GHz, configured with 4 vCPUs across 2 physical cores and 2 threads per core. The processor includes 48 KB L1d cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 105 MB L3 cache. It is equipped with 8.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 5 GHz, yielding a 2.0 GB per core memory allocation. This instance does not include local storage or a GPU, and it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate average single-core performance, with a stress-ng single-core score of 2032.08 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1912.0. However, multi-core and memory-bound performance metrics are generally weak. The stress-ng multi-core score is 4216.75, and the Geekbench multi-core score is 4231.0. Memory bandwidth is a notable bottleneck, with a poor Passmark memory score of 978.31 and weak read-only large block memory bandwidth at 25.92 GB/sec. Despite these memory constraints, the server exhibits average performance in single-threaded gzip compression (30.35 GB/sec) and static web serving throughput (7.82 GB/sec).

The c7i-flex.xlarge offers a resource-dense, compute-focused profile with a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, making it a qualitatively cost-efficient option for workloads that require modern Intel CPU instruction sets, such as AVX-512 and AMX, without the high memory footprint of standard instances. Tradeoffs include weak multi-threaded scaling, low memory bandwidth, and the absence of local storage. This server is best aligned with light compute tasks, single-threaded processing, static web serving, and basic text processing workloads.
